title: Redwood discovery — model selection (Bluehaven Logistics)
summary: Intro discovery with Bluehaven Logistics focused on model selection for multi-lingual customer support and long-context supply-chain documents. Customer weighing Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private — concerns around latency, cost, data residency, KMS, and tool-calling integrations. Agreed next steps: pricing + dedicated sizing, security docs, schedule technical deep-dive and benchmark run with representative prompts and 64k/32k context tests.
action_items: Sarah Kim: send tailored pricing and Dedicated sizing estimate by 2026-04-02
Daniel Ortiz: schedule technical deep dive and benchmarking run; include instructions to run sample workload and provide on-prem pilot checklist by 2026-04-06
Priya Nair: share representative prompt set and dataset samples (anonymized) by 2026-04-01
Marta Ruiz: list of compliance questions (SOC2/ISO/SAML/KMS) to be sent to Redwood security by 2026-04-03
next_steps: Share security whitepaper and SOC2 report link
Schedule SE deep-dive and benchmark run
Set up 2-week on-prem/private pilot scope if Dedicated sizing looks good
transcript:
Header: 2026-03-30 14:00 PDT | Duration 56m | Attendees: Sarah Kim (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Bluehaven Head of ML), Ethan Cole (Platform), Marta Ruiz (Security), Lucas Tan (Product)

[00:00] Sarah: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intros? I'm Sarah Kim, account exec on the Redwood side.
[00:07] Priya: Hi, Priya here, Head of ML at Bluehaven. We're trying to pick models and deployment—long context stuff, multilingual customer messages.
[00:14] Daniel: Daniel Ortiz, solutions engineer, I'll take the deep technical questions on latency, batching, KV cache and tool-calling.
[00:20] Ethan: Ethan, platform eng, I'll own infra constraints — VPC, network egress, etc.
[00:24] Marta: Marta from security, I'll be asking compliance and encryption Qs.
[00:27] Lucas: Lucas, product — mainly use cases and timelines.
[00:30] Sarah: Great. Quick agenda: understand your use cases, constraints, then model + deployment options (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), and agree next steps.
[00:38] Priya: Our main application is a customer support assistant plus long-form document summarization for shipping manifests — sometimes docs up to 30k tokens. Also need multilingual support: English, Spanish, Portuguese, a little Japanese. Tool-calling is important — needs to call internal APIs and retrieve customer account info.
[00:55] Daniel: Got it. So two high-level reqs: long context (30k+), multilingual, and tool-calling with secure access. Quick question on latency SLOs?
[01:02] Lucas: For support chat, target p50 < 500ms for short prompts, p95 under 1.2s ideally. For batch summarization it's okay if it's a few seconds.
[01:12] Ethan: We also need to avoid cross-customer data leakage; data residency for EU customers would be nice.
[01:18] Marta: And we require SOC2, SSO (SAML) and KMS integration for key management. Also retention policies.
[01:25] Sarah: Thanks. On models — we're recommending evaluating a few open models: Redwood-optimized variants (we have verified profiles), and others like Anthropic or OpenAI hosted models you may be comparing. For long context and multilingual, some models have 32k or 64k context variants; others require chunking or retrieval augmentation. Which is more important: native long context or lower cost with retrieval?
[01:47] Priya: Native long context would simplify things. Our summarization must preserve order and referential integrity across docs. Retrieval adds complexity.
[01:56] Daniel: Understood. On Redwood Hosted, you can use our 32k and 64k model variants (depending on availability) with streaming and tool-calling. Hosted is fastest to get started, pay-as-you-go. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools — better tail latency and predictable throughput, and you can pin specific quantized variants for cost. Private (VPC/on-prem) is for when you need full network isolation and customer-managed keys.
[02:20] Ethan: If we go Dedicated, can we still do private networking? Like VPC peering?
[02:24] Daniel: Yes, Dedicated supports private network connections and can be deployed into customer VPCs in some cases; Private is a fuller option where the control plane is customer-managed. There's a difference in responsibility model.
[02:34] Marta: For KMS — do you support customer-managed keys and HSM?
[02:37] Daniel: Yes, we integrate with major KMS providers and HSM for Private deployments; Hosted supports encrypted-at-rest with platform keys but we also offer bring-your-own-key options for enterprise tiers. We'll share the security whitepaper.
[02:49] Priya: About model quality: how do Redwood-verified models compare multilingually? Spanish and Portuguese fidelity is critical; Japanese is lower priority.
[02:58] Daniel: Our verified models include evaluation profiles across languages and tasks. Typically 7B-13B quantized models can handle multilingual basics, but for higher fidelity, a 70B+ model or specific multilingual-pretrained models are better. For 30k token contexts, larger models or specialized long-context variants perform better. We can run a quick benchmark on your representative prompts.
[03:18] Lucas: Cost is also a factor — we have a tight budget. How does quantization affect cost vs quality?
[03:24] Daniel: Quantization reduces GPU memory and allows more throughput per GPU, lowering cost. There's usually a small hit to quality. Our Optimize tooling recommends quantization profiles by workload; we can show tradeoff curves from previous benchmarks.
[03:36] Priya: Tool-calling — we need secure function calls that fetch account data and call internal microservices. Can we restrict exposures?
[03:42] Daniel: Yes, you can use function/tool calling with access tokens that are short-lived, and RBAC controls in the console to limit which routes can call which tools. For Private, you can run the tool adapters inside your VPC so data never leaves your network.
[03:56] Ethan: Are there examples of customers doing on-prem tool adapters?
[03:59] Daniel: A handful of our enterprise customers run adapter microservices in their VPC and use SQS/Kafka for eventing — we have a reference architecture we can share.
[04:08] Marta: Can you send SOC2 and ISO artifacts? We'll need them for procurement.
[04:12] Sarah: Absolutely — I'll attach the security pack.
[04:14] Priya: For benchmarking, we want to test: 1) chat short-turn latency, 2) 30k doc summarization end-to-end, 3) multilingual accuracy on a labeled subset. Also tool-calling with redaction rules.
[04:29] Daniel: Good plan. We'll propose a benchmark harness: sample prompts you provide, run across 3 model variants (quantized medium, 13B/70B equivalents, and 64k long context variant if available), measure latency, token cost, and quality metrics.
[04:44] Lucas: Timeline — we're aiming for a pilot in Q2. Is that feasible?
[04:48] Sarah: Yes, feasible. If we get requirements and samples this week, we can scope a 2-week pilot in mid-April.
[04:56] Priya: About data residency — EU traffic must stay in eu-west region; can that be guaranteed on Hosted?
[05:02] Daniel: Hosted can run regionally; we have EU regions. For guaranteed isolation and customer-owned networking, Dedicated or Private might be preferable. We'll map options in the follow-up.
[05:12] Marta: Logging/audit — we need audit logs for function calls and data access. Do you provide token-level tracing?
[05:18] Daniel: Yes, our Console has per-route tracing, token-level cost and latency breakdowns, and audit logs. For Private, logs can be shipped to your SIEM.
[05:26] Ethan: One more infra question: how much engineering work to integrate SAML SSO and provision RBAC?
[05:31] Sarah: Usually a few days to configure SAML and roles; we support SCIM for user provisioning. We'll share the SAML guides.
[05:38] Priya: Any hard limits on request rate for Hosted? We expect spiky loads during peak return periods.
[05:44] Daniel: Hosted has rate limits; Dedicated offers reserved throughput and autoscaling policies with burst capacity options. For spiky workloads, Dedicated or Reserved capacity is safer for predictable tail latency.
[05:55] Lucas: Are there fallback strategies if our primary model is overloaded?
[05:58] Daniel: Yes, smart routing supports fallbacks to compatible model variants and region-based routing. You can define policies at route level for graceful degradation.
[06:06] Priya: Ok — the three main blockers for us: 1) cost estimate for required throughput, 2) security + KMS confirmation, 3) benchmark results on our prompts.
[06:16] Sarah: Action plan: I'll send pricing and security docs; Daniel will schedule the benchmark and provide a runbook; Priya will send prompt sets and anonymized docs. We'll aim to reconvene after the benchmark.
[06:25] Marta: We'll also send a list of compliance questions.
[06:28] Sarah: Great. Any other questions?
[06:30] Ethan: Not from infra.
[06:31] Lucas: None from product.
[06:32] Priya: No. Thanks, looking forward to the benchmark.
[06:34] Sarah: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the packet and calendar invites.
[06:37] (call ends)
